q01.key_idea: Count only the triangles in each box.
steps: Look at each box and count just the triangles. Skip the circles and squares.
Box A has 1 triangle, box B has 4, box C has 2, box D has 3 and box E has 1.
4 is the biggest number, so box B has the most triangles.

choice_feedback.A: Box A has only 1 triangle. Most of its shapes are circles and squares.
choice_feedback.D: Box D has 3 triangles. That is 1 fewer than box B.

q02.key_idea: The second order is the first order plus one more juice.
steps: Both orders have one sandwich.
The second order has one more juice than the first order.
That one extra juice makes the price go up from 12 to 14 Euros.
14 - 12 = 2, so one juice costs 2 Euros.

choice_feedback.A: If a juice cost 1 Euro, the second order would cost 12 + 1 = 13 Euros, not 14.
choice_feedback.C: If a juice cost 3 Euros, the second order would cost 12 + 3 = 15 Euros, not 14.
choice_feedback.D: If a juice cost 4 Euros, the second order would cost 12 + 4 = 16 Euros, not 14.
choice_feedback.E: If a juice cost 5 Euros, the second order would cost 12 + 5 = 17 Euros, not 14.

q03.key_idea: The new picture must use one left half and one right half of the mushroom.
steps: The cut makes a left half and a right half. They are mirror pictures of each other.
On the left half, the round edges of the cap and the stem bulge out to the left. On the right half, they bulge out to the right.
Turning a piece upside down does not change which half it is.
In picture E, the left piece is the left half standing up, and the right piece is the right half turned upside down. That is one of each.

choice_feedback.A: Both pieces are left halves. Anna has only one left half.
choice_feedback.B: The upside-down piece is a left half too, so this picture uses two left halves.
choice_feedback.C: Both pieces are left halves. One of them is just turned upside down.
choice_feedback.D: Both pieces are left halves turned upside down.

q04.key_idea: Find the row with only 1 coin and the column with only 1 coin.
steps: Count the coins in each row from the top: 2, 2, 1, 2. The third row needs one more coin.
Count the coins in each column from the left: 2, 2, 1, 2. The third column needs one more coin.
The new coin must go in the third row and the third column. That square is D.

choice_feedback.A: Square A is in the second row, which already has 2 coins.
choice_feedback.B: Square B is in the top row, which already has 2 coins.
choice_feedback.C: Square C is in the second row, which already has 2 coins.
choice_feedback.E: Square E is in the bottom row, which already has 2 coins.

q05.key_idea: The torn piece must fit the corner, and the things on it must carry on from the map.
steps: The tear is at the top right corner of the map. So the piece has a straight top edge and a straight right edge.
Turn piece B upside down. Its two straight edges become a top edge and a right edge, and its torn edge fits the tear.
On the map, the red dashed path runs up toward the torn corner. On piece B, the red path carries on and ends at the treasure X.
The other pieces only show things we can already see on the map, like ships, mountains, the skull and the fish skeleton.

choice_feedback.A: The ships and mountains on this piece are already on the map.
choice_feedback.C: The fish skeleton on this piece is already on the map.
choice_feedback.D: The two people and the mountains on this piece are already on the map.
choice_feedback.E: The skull on this piece is already on the map.

q06.key_idea: Look for a shape that shows up on just one animal.
steps: Every animal has triangles, so a triangle is not the special shape.
Squares and slanted pieces show up on more than one animal too.
The purple animal has a long rectangle for its head. It is twice as long as it is tall.
No other animal has a rectangle like that. It is on animal D.

choice_feedback.A: Every shape on this animal is also used on another animal.
choice_feedback.B: Every shape on this animal is also used on another animal.
choice_feedback.C: Every shape on this animal is also used on another animal.
choice_feedback.E: Every shape on this animal is also used on another animal.

q07.key_idea: First find the two baskets that match in both pattern and shape.
steps: Baskets 2 and 4 look the same: the same dotted pattern and the same shape. The koala and the fox sleep there.
Baskets 1 and 3 have the same woven pattern, but their shapes are different. The kangaroo and the rabbit sleep there.
Only basket 5 is left, so the mouse sleeps in basket 5.

choice_feedback.A: Basket 1 has the same pattern as basket 3, so the kangaroo or the rabbit sleeps there.
choice_feedback.B: Basket 2 matches basket 4, so the koala or the fox sleeps there.
choice_feedback.C: Basket 3 has the same pattern as basket 1, so the kangaroo or the rabbit sleeps there.
choice_feedback.D: Basket 4 matches basket 2, so the koala or the fox sleeps there.

q08.key_idea: Check the blocks one by one and count the blocks each one touches.
steps: On the left, 3 long blocks lie flat, one on top of the other. On the right, 2 long blocks stand up, one behind the other.
Each standing block touches all 3 flat blocks and the other standing block. That is 4.
The middle flat block touches the block above it, the block below it and both standing blocks. That is 4.
The top flat block and the bottom flat block each touch the middle flat block and both standing blocks. That is 3.
So 2 blocks touch exactly 3 others.

choice_feedback.A: The top flat block and the bottom flat block both touch exactly 3 others, so there are more than 1.
choice_feedback.C: The middle flat block touches 4 others, not 3.
choice_feedback.D: The two standing blocks touch 4 others, not 3.
choice_feedback.E: Only the top and bottom flat blocks touch exactly 3 others.

q09.key_idea: Follow each path arrow by arrow and stop if it lands in water.
steps: The kangaroo starts in the bottom left corner. The koala is in the top right corner.
Path C goes 2 right, 2 up, 2 right, 2 up, then 3 right.
Those jumps go around all 4 ponds and land right on the koala.

choice_feedback.A: After 2 jumps right and 3 jumps up, the kangaroo lands in the pond at the top.
choice_feedback.B: After 2 jumps right, 2 jumps up and 4 more jumps right, the kangaroo lands in the pond on the right.
choice_feedback.D: The first jump to the left at the end lands in the pond at the top.
choice_feedback.E: After 2 jumps right and 3 jumps up, the kangaroo lands in the pond at the top.

q10.key_idea: The same shape hides the same digit, and different shapes hide different digits.
steps: The shapes are: heart, diamond, diamond, club, spade.
Only the 2nd and 3rd shapes are the same. So the 2nd and 3rd digits must be the same, and all the other digits must be different.
34426: the 2nd and 3rd digits are both 4, and 3, 4, 2, 6 are all different. It fits.

choice_feedback.B: 34526 has 4 and 5 under the two diamonds, but the same shape needs the same digit.
choice_feedback.C: 34423 has 3 under the heart and under the spade, but those are different shapes.
choice_feedback.D: 34424 has 4 under the spade too, but the spade is not a diamond.
choice_feedback.E: 32446 has 2 and 4 under the two diamonds, but the same shape needs the same digit.

q11.key_idea: The path is made of 4 strips, one on each side, and each strip is 1 longer than the side of the square.
steps: Look at the pictures: each strip of the path runs along one side and pokes out 1 past a corner.
Side 1: each strip is 1 + 1 = 2 long, so it takes 1 stone. 4 strips take 4 stones.
Side 3: each strip is 3 + 1 = 4 long, so it takes 2 stones. 4 strips take 8 stones.
Side 5: each strip is 5 + 1 = 6 long, so it takes 3 stones. 4 strips take 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 12 stones.

choice_feedback.A: Each of the 4 sides needs 3 stones, which makes 12. 10 stones are too few.
choice_feedback.B: Each of the 4 sides needs 3 stones, which makes 12. 11 stones are too few.
choice_feedback.D: Each of the 4 sides needs 3 stones, which makes 12. 14 stones are too many.
choice_feedback.E: 16 stones would be 4 stones on each side, but each side needs only 3.

q12.key_idea: Count the small triangles in each lawn.
steps: The dots make a grid of small triangles. Every lawn is made of these small triangles.
Count them: lawn A has 7, lawn B has 8, lawn C has 8, lawn D has 8 and lawn E has 8.
7 is the smallest number, so lawn A has the least grass.

choice_feedback.B: Lawn B has 8 small triangles. That is 1 more than lawn A.
choice_feedback.C: Lawn C has 8 small triangles. That is 1 more than lawn A.
choice_feedback.D: Lawn D has 8 small triangles. That is 1 more than lawn A.
choice_feedback.E: Lawn E has 8 small triangles. That is 1 more than lawn A.

q13.key_idea: The two empty circles in the middle belong to both houses.
steps: The left house has 6, 2 and 5. 6 + 2 + 5 = 13.
So the two empty middle circles must make 20 - 13 = 7 together.
The right house uses the same two middle circles, so they give 7 there too. With 3 and 1: 7 + 3 + 1 = 11.
20 - 11 = 9, so the question mark is 9.

choice_feedback.A: With 3, the right house adds up to 7 + 3 + 1 + 3 = 14, not 20.
choice_feedback.B: With 4, the right house adds up to 7 + 3 + 1 + 4 = 15, not 20.
choice_feedback.C: With 7, the right house adds up to 7 + 3 + 1 + 7 = 18, not 20.
choice_feedback.E: With 14, the right house adds up to 7 + 3 + 1 + 14 = 25, not 20.

q14.key_idea: Dino cannot walk through every room, so leave out the smallest room he has to.
steps: All 8 rooms together make 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 + 7 + 8 = 36.
Colour the rooms like a chessboard. Each step goes to a room of the other colour. Room 1 and room 8 have the same colour, so Dino always has to leave out a room of the other colour: 2, 4, 5 or 7.
Leave out the smallest one, room 2. Dino walks 1, 5, 6, 7, 3, 4, 8.
1 + 5 + 6 + 7 + 3 + 4 + 8 = 34. That is the biggest result.

choice_feedback.E: 36 means walking through all 8 rooms, and Dino cannot do that from room 1 to room 8.

q15.key_idea: Work out each zebra's stripes, then pick the biggest number.
steps: Runa has 15 stripes.
Zara has 3 more than Runa: 15 + 3 = 18.
Runa has 5 less than Biba, so Biba has 5 more than Runa: 15 + 5 = 20.
20 is the most, so Biba wins with 20 stripes.

choice_feedback.A: No zebra has 16 stripes. Runa has 15, Zara has 18 and Biba has 20.
choice_feedback.B: 18 is Zara's number, but Biba has more stripes.
choice_feedback.D: No zebra has 21 stripes. Biba has 15 + 5 = 20.
choice_feedback.E: No zebra has 22 stripes. Biba has 15 + 5 = 20.
